stem: A project has models, tests, snapshots, and seeds. A developer currently runs `dbt seed`, then `dbt snapshot`, then `dbt run`, then `dbt test`, as four separate invocations. The developer wants one command that runs all of these resource types together, respecting the DAG so a failing upstream resource skips its downstream dependents. Which single command replaces the four, and why?

option_texts.A: `dbt build`, because it runs models, tests, snapshots, and seeds together in DAG order for the selected resources
option_texts.B: `dbt run`, because run also executes tests and snapshots together with models once they finish
option_texts.C: `dbt compile`, because compiling the project triggers every resource type to execute afterward
option_texts.D: `dbt docs generate`, because generating docs also builds every resource type it documents

drill_answer_short: dbt build runs models, tests, snapshots, and seeds together in DAG order
decision_hinge: The dbt build command will run models, test tests, snapshot snapshots, and seed seeds, in DAG order, for selected resources or an entire project.

plausible_options.B: wants one command that runs all of these resource types together

eliminated_by.C: respecting the DAG so a failing upstream resource skips its downstream dependents

D.signal: wants one command that runs all of these resource types together
D.requires_fact: The dbt build command will run models, test tests, snapshot snapshots, and seed seeds, in DAG order, for selected resources or an entire project.

distractor_traps.B: T3: confusable sibling — dbt run only builds models, it does not also execute tests, snapshots, or seeds
distractor_traps.C: T1: fabricated — dbt compile does not execute any resource against the warehouse
distractor_traps.D: T1: fabricated — generating docs does not build any resource

stem: After running `dbt docs generate` and opening the generated site, a new team member clicks into the lineage graph for `fct_orders` to understand the pipeline before making a change. What information does that lineage graph actually show them?

option_texts.A: A DAG of the project showing how models, sources, and other resources connect to and depend on each other
option_texts.B: The Git commit history of the project, showing how `fct_orders` has changed release over release
option_texts.C: Row-level lineage, tracing which individual source rows produced each row currently in `fct_orders`
option_texts.D: Real-time warehouse query activity for every model that is currently running

drill_answer_short: The lineage graph is a DAG of how project resources connect to and depend on each other
decision_hinge: dbt generates documentation for your project using descriptions and commands. The documentation for your project includes information about your project, including model code, a DAG of your project, any tests you've added to a column, and more.

plausible_options.C: to understand the pipeline before making a change

B.requires_fact: dbt documentation includes a DAG of your project generated from model code and dependencies, not a record of git commit history.

eliminated_by.D: After running `dbt docs generate` and opening the generated site

distractor_traps.B: T1: fabricated — the generated site documents the project's resources and dependencies, not its git history
distractor_traps.C: T8: scope error — the graph shows resource-level dependencies, not row-level provenance
distractor_traps.D: T1: fabricated — the generated docs site is a static artifact, not a live query monitor

stem: A team wants their dbt docs site to be genuinely useful to new analysts, not just technically present. Which TWO documented practices actually improve the generated documentation?

option_texts.A: Add descriptions to models, columns, and sources so the docs site explains what each one means
option_texts.B: Use `{% docs %}` blocks for long-form descriptions and reference them with `{{ doc(...) }}` in schema.yml, keeping schema.yml concise
option_texts.C: Rename every model file to exactly match its database schema name, since the docs site organizes pages by file name
option_texts.D: Disable `persist_docs` everywhere, since descriptions only need to live in the dbt docs site

drill_answer_short: Add descriptions, and use docs blocks with doc() to keep schema.yml readable
decision_hinge: dbt provides a way to add descriptions to models, columns, sources, and more, to further enhance your documentation. To use a docs block, reference it from your schema.yml file with the doc() function in place of a markdown string.

plausible_options.D: genuinely useful to new analysts, not just technically present

eliminated_by.C: genuinely useful to new analysts, not just technically present

distractor_traps.C: T1: fabricated — the docs site is not organized by matching file names to schema names
distractor_traps.D: T8: scope error — persist_docs writes descriptions into the warehouse as comments; it does not control the docs site itself

stem: A project sets `persist_docs: {relation: true, columns: true}` on a group of models. The analytics engineer needs to know what actually changes in the warehouse once this config is applied and the models are rebuilt. What happens?

option_texts.A: dbt writes the model and column descriptions as relation and column comments directly in the database
option_texts.B: dbt generates markdown documentation files on disk for every affected model
option_texts.C: dbt enforces the described column types as constraints at build time
option_texts.D: Nothing changes in the database; persist_docs only affects the generated docs site

drill_answer_short: persist_docs writes descriptions as column and relation comments in the database
decision_hinge: persist_docs optionally persists resource descriptions as column and relation comments in the database. By default, documentation persistence is disabled.

plausible_options.D: needs to know what actually changes in the warehouse once this config is applied

eliminated_by.B: needs to know what actually changes in the warehouse once this config is applied

C.signal: needs to know what actually changes in the warehouse once this config is applied
C.requires_fact: persist_docs optionally persists resource descriptions as column and relation comments in the database; it does not enforce column types as constraints.

distractor_traps.B: T1: fabricated — persist_docs writes comments into the database, not markdown files to disk
distractor_traps.C: T3: confusable sibling — enforcing column types is what a model contract does, not persist_docs
distractor_traps.D: T3: confusable sibling — persist_docs changes the database directly; it is independent of the docs site refresh

stem: A project keeps diagrams in an `assets/` folder at the project root and wants those image files copied into the generated docs site when `dbt docs generate` runs, without dbt treating them as models or other resources. Which config accomplishes this, and why?

option_texts.A: `asset-paths: ['assets']` in `dbt_project.yml`, because it copies the listed directories into the target directory as part of docs generate
option_texts.B: `model-paths: ['assets']`, because any directory listed there is copied into the docs site
option_texts.C: `docs-paths: ['assets']`, since documentation-related folders need their own dedicated config key
option_texts.D: Nothing extra is needed, because `dbt docs generate` copies every project folder into the target directory by default

drill_answer_short: asset-paths copies listed directories into the target directory during docs generate
decision_hinge: asset-paths optionally specifies a custom list of directories to copy to the target directory as part of the docs generate command. By default, dbt will not copy any additional files as part of docs generate.

plausible_options.B: wants those image files copied into the generated docs site when `dbt docs generate` runs

eliminated_by.C: without dbt treating them as models or other resources

D.signal: wants those image files copied into the generated docs site
D.requires_fact: By default, dbt will not copy any additional files as part of docs generate.

distractor_traps.B: T3: confusable sibling — model-paths tells dbt where to look for model files, not which folders to copy for docs
distractor_traps.C: T1: fabricated — dbt defines no docs-paths config key
distractor_traps.D: T4: breaks a stated requirement — dbt copies no additional files by default, so the images would not appear

stem: A team writes a long paragraph describing `fct_orders` inside a `{% docs fct_orders_overview %} ... {% enddocs %}` block in a `.md` file, and wants that text to appear as the model's description in `schema.yml` without retyping it. Which syntax in `schema.yml` pulls in that block's content?

option_texts.D: List the block's name under a `docs:` property, and schema.yml inlines it automatically

drill_answer_short: Reference a docs block from schema.yml with the doc() function
decision_hinge: To use a docs block, reference it from your schema.yml file with the doc() function in place of a markdown string.

plausible_options.C: inside a `{% docs fct_orders_overview %} ... {% enddocs %}` block

eliminated_by.B: wants that text to appear as the model's description in `schema.yml`

D.signal: wants that text to appear as the model's description in `schema.yml` without retyping it
D.requires_fact: To use a docs block, reference it from your schema.yml file with the doc() function in place of a markdown string.

distractor_traps.B: T3: confusable sibling — ref() resolves a model, seed, or snapshot, not a markdown docs block
distractor_traps.C: T3: confusable sibling — that tag defines a docs block, it does not reference one from schema.yml
distractor_traps.D: T1: fabricated — schema.yml has no automatic docs: property
